biggest_gap.what: Round 11 gave every person in Black Marsh their own stand and it worked. It also froze every one of them in it. MEASURED IN THE RUNNING GAME, not read out of the source: at the Lilmoth stand, reading each drawn actor's bone rotations twice sixty frames — one second — apart, **0 of 60 NPCs change any non-foot bone by any amount, and the worst change across the whole crowd is exactly 0 radians**. The required-to-disagree control in the same session is the player, whose bones move 0.011246 m over the same interval. The cause is not a defect in the stand and the stand should not be touched: `render/actor.js:poseStatic` solves each person's stance ONCE (`if (A.staticStance === undefined)`) and caches it, and each person's place in the 96-frame breathing loop is a per-person CONSTANT dealt by `stanceVariationFor`. Nothing re-evaluates it, so the only thing that changes on this path from one frame to the next is the two-bone terrain conform. THE BUILD PUBLISHED THIS ITSELF AND READ IT THE OTHER WAY UP: its live arm L2 reports worst non-foot drift of 2.842e-12 m over 37 frames and files it as proof the stance is stable. It is that, and it is also proof that a settlement is a waxworks. RI-VIS10 C3 arm (a) has always required that 'the two frames differ'; the crowd arm the r10 critic added inherited every other clause from arm (a) and not that one, so a town of 408 motionless figures in 392 distinct poses scores 100%.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: A player walking into Lilmoth now sees sixty people standing in different attitudes, which is a genuine and photographed improvement over sixty copies of one mannequin — and then sees that not one of them draws breath, shifts weight, or turns their head, for as long as they care to watch. Stillness is the faster tell of the two: a viewer notices that nothing in a market moves before they notice that everybody in it is posed the same. This is also the cheapest remaining thing in the item by a wide margin, because the hard parts — a per-person seeded distribution, a numerically solved root drop, a presentation bind against the posed frame, and a caching strategy — are all already built and all measured correct.
biggest_gap.remedy: In `game/src/render/actor.js`, split `applyStaticStance`'s one-time solve into the part that is genuinely per-person-constant and the part that is a function of the loop frame. Cache the seeded `stanceVariationFor(name)` record on `A.staticStance` as now, and re-run only the `stance.loop.applyPose(buf, V.loopFrame + t)` / `addPose` / `mirrorPose` / `addVariation` / root-solve sequence on a staggered cadence — `t` advancing with the renderer's frame counter and the crowd split into N buckets so at most 408/N actors re-solve on any one frame. N = 8 gives every person a fresh pose eight times a second at one eighth of the per-frame cost, which is the same trade `syncNPCs` already makes for the terrain conform. DONE MEANS: (1) `corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-F10-r11-critic/frozen-crowd.json`'s probe, re-run, reports >= 90% of drawn NPCs with a changed non-foot bone rotation between two frames 60 apart — arm (b2) of the amended C3; and (2) the same probe still reports the PLAYER control moving, so a green (1) cannot be bought by breaking the reader. PRESERVATION PER S59, all four required, and they are what stop (1) being bought by re-rolling the crowd every frame: (a) arm (b1) stays >= 90% on the drawn population — variety must not be traded for motion; (b) each named individual's stance must remain a pure function of their eid, i.e. the REBUILD, TRAVEL and SAVE/RELOAD arms of `tools/visual/f10-r11c-stance-probe.mjs` must still return 60 of 60 bit-identical, because a crowd that re-rolls on stream-in is a worse defect than a crowd that is still; (c) the lower ankle stays within 1 mm of its current per-person value — the numeric root solve must be re-run with the pose, not left behind at the old phase, or the whole crowd hovers again; (d) `node tools/harness/anim-tune.mjs` still reports 0 of 14 over 0.35 m with worst snapOut <= 0.0122 m. AND ONE BUDGET CLAUSE, because this is the only remedy in this item with a per-frame cost: publish the frame time at the Lilmoth stand before and after, and it must not rise by more than 5%.

corpus_extended.why: F10 r11's first and largest admission is that its pictures did not land, and it files the cause as a harness defect that would block every future settlement capture and asks ring 0 for a new method. There is no such defect: drawn NPC world x and z equal the simulation's to 0.000000 on 60 of 60 matched pairs, `province.group.position` and `scene.position` are both the origin, and the three.js camera position equals the sim camera's to every printed digit. A CENSUS DEFECT BOTH THE r10 VERDICT AND THIS ROUND INHERITED, AND IT IS WHY THE ROUND'S CAMERA FOUND A ROOFTOP. At the Lilmoth stand `sim.npcs` holds 60 records and the renderer builds 60 meshes — but **29 of them have `mesh.visible === false`, and all 29 sit within 5 m of the WORLD ORIGIN on ground y between -41.134 and -40.703 m**, i.e. under the Topal. Four more ARE visible, at approximately (4906, -594) on ground -33 m, which is outside the province's own x extent. **The drawn-and-in-settlement crowd at that stand is 27.** So 'C3 arm (b) fails 0 of 60' (r10) and 'C3 arm (b) passes 60 of 60' (r11) are both computed over a denominator that is 55% figures no player can ever see, against an arm whose own words are 'DRAWN NPCs'. THE FINDING DOES NOT OVERTURN THE ROUND'S RESULT AND I CHECKED THAT FIRST: recomputed on every denominator, arm (b1) reads 60 of 60 over all meshes, 31 of 31 over the visible, and 27 of 27 over the visible-and-local. THE BRIEF ASKED ME TO TEST THE CONSTRUCTION RATHER THAN THE CLAIM, SO I RAN THE THREE THINGS THE BUILD'S OWN EVIDENCE STRUCTURALLY COULD NOT SEE — its stability arms are all WITHIN one session. (A) REBUILD: every NPC mesh destroyed and rebuilt by `syncNPCs` — **60 of 60 bone-rotation signatures bit-identical**. (B) TRAVEL: teleported ~2.4 km away to another settlement, 30 frames, back — **60 of 60 identical**. (C) SAVE / RELOAD: `saveState()` then `loadState()` then back to the same stand — **60 of 60 identical**. A person's stand is a pure function of their `eid` and the `eid` is authored, so it survives the three ways a seeded distribution normally breaks. On body-hash independence: the two seeds are the FNV-1a of two different strings (`npc:<eid>` and `stance:npc:<eid>`), they collide on 0 of 408 eids, and grouping the 408 by their body-pool index gives mean stance depths of 0.900 to 0.971 against an overall 0.936 with no clustering — the stance a person is dealt does not track the body they are dealt.

TWO HALVES, AND THEY GO OPPOSITE WAYS. **The shipped path IS consumed, and I proved it the way RI-MTH07 demands** — by perturbing the model and watching the drawn thing change, with a null control. NULL CONTROL: an unread field added to the live `idle_ready` stance object, every NPC mesh rebuilt — **60 of 60 identical**, so the instrument is not merely reporting that rebuilding changes things. PERTURB: every rotation key in that same shipped stance tripled, meshes rebuilt — **60 of 60 CHANGED**. That is a proper consumption pass and the round earned it. **But the round's framing of WHY the recovered work needed this round is wrong, and its own file contains the refutation.** Its headline is *'The quarantined `actor.js` was INERT … nothing anywhere passed it — `grep -n poseStatic game/src/render/renderer.js` returned three calls with five arguments'*, filed as *'`RI-MTH07`'s consumption defect exactly … the fourth instance this project has found'*. Checked on the quarantine commit itself: `git show 86181c27:game/src/render/renderer.js` contains `_anyStance` at line 697 and passes `stance` to `poseStatic` at lines 735 and 812. **The quarantine was not inert; it shipped its own caller.** The round declined that file and wrote its own — which it says, in `recovered_and_NOT_used`, two entries above the headline that contradicts it. The true and much smaller statement is that the SUBSET the round chose to recover was inert until it wired it, which is a fact about a partial recovery and not an instance of a rule with no caller. JOB 3, RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY — I imported `game/src/combat/swing.js` and `clips.js` directly rather than re-running the round's instrument, and enumerated the registry myself. `Object.keys(clip-registry.json.clips).length` = **1160**. Phase 0 of the root-offset curve BEFORE: **exactly 0 on 1,160 of 1,160 — one distinct value**. AFTER: **-0.008 on 1,160 of 1,160**. Boundary step against the idle's -0.00796: **0.00796 m -> 0.00004 m**. So every weapon attack in the game did begin and end with a 7.96 mm vertical pop and now does not, and `anim-tune`'s fourteen archetype rows genuinely could not see it. **AND THE PRESERVATION ARM IS STRUCTURAL, NOT STATISTICAL, WHICH IS BETTER THAN THE ROUND CLAIMED FOR ITSELF.** The round reports max delta 0 inside phase 1.0-2.0 from a 601-point sample, which a critic is entitled to read as 'the grid missed it'. It cannot have: `clips.js:29 sampleCurve` interpolates between ADJACENT keys only (piecewise smoothstep), the stance term is added to the keys at phase 0.0 and 3.0 alone, the keys at 1.0 and 2.0 are untouched, and **0 of 1,160 clips carry any key strictly inside (1, 2)**. The active window cannot depend on the endpoints. Since `Clip.phaseAt` maps the active frames of every attack onto exactly that band, the hit window, `peak_tip_speed_mps`, `calibrateExcursion` and `_bladeLength` are provably unchanged, and my independent `anim-tune` re-run confirms the boundary gate at snapIn 0.0000 x14 and worst snapOut 0.0122 m. It is bounded to the anticipation and the settle by the same structural argument, and the right fix is the one the round names: the stance belongs in the data those tools load, not in a constructor argument.
